title: ASP.NET Core · Why Middleware Order Matters

scenes.line2: What happens if you get it wrong?
scenes.say: Why does the order of middleware in ASP.NET Core matter so much? What happens if you get it wrong?

scenes.label: Pipeline
scenes.sub: Requests flow through middleware, each can modify or handle.
scenes.say: Every request flows through a pipeline of middleware. Each middleware can handle or modify the request and response.
Order matters. Authentication should run before authorization, and logging can wrap everything to record details.
In Program dot C S, add authentication before authorization. This ensures users are identified before access is checked.

scenes.question: What happens if auth runs after authorization?
scenes.right: Authorization fails because user identity isn't set yet.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: What happens if authentication runs after authorization? Authorization fails, because the user identity isn't set yet.
